input.quote: b) The total liability for either Party, regardless of the form of action, whether contract or tort, is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials contained in the Products delivered to IBM and IBM Customers by MSL in the period beginning with the Effective Date of the Agreement through the resolution of the action.
input.rationale: Section 15.3 caps both Parties (mutual, satisfying that element) and mutually excludes consequential damages in 15.3(a), but it fails the fallback on two material terms: the cap basis is 3% of the bill-of-materials value of Products delivered over the whole life of the Agreement rather than 12 months' fees, and there are no carve-outs at all — MSL's Section 15.1 indemnities (including IP infringement), confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside this small cap, which is expressly walk-away territory. The redline keeps the existing mutual sentence and changes only the basis to fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim and adds the four fallback carve-outs. The Equipment and Program Loan Agreement § 15 ($25,000 cap on IBM's liability to MSL) runs in our favour and is not flagged.

proposal.summary: Change § 15.3(b) cap basis to 12 months' fees and carve out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap based on the fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct sitting outside the cap; a 3% bill-of-materials cap with no carve-outs would put MSL's indemnities under Section 15.1 inside an illusory cap. We have kept the mutual structure of the existing sentence and changed only the basis and the carve-outs.

ops.newText: is limited to the fees paid or payable by IBM to MSL under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim; provided that this limitation does not apply to either Party's indemnification obligations, breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence, or willful misconduct.
